lines.text: How far to the next place with a roof on it?
Further than you want to hear. Same as yesterday.
You've gone quiet.
I'm walking. It's difficult to do both properly.
Do you ever think about what you'd be doing, if none of this had come along?
Every day. It's mostly bread. I'd be making bread, and I'd be good at it.
...I'd come to that shop.
Something's been keeping pace with us since the ridge.
I know. Don't turn round. It stops being curious the moment we look interested.
{b}. If I go down out here, don't drag me home. Put me somewhere with a view.
You'd only complain about the view.
Then pick a good one and I'll have nothing to say.
I've stopped counting the days.
I stopped the week I met you. On the whole it's been an improvement.
You take the left side now without being asked. Did you notice you'd started doing that?
No.
Neither did I, for about a month.
You walked us straight past the turning.
I walked us past nothing. There was no turning. There was a tree you liked.
Must you breathe like that?
It's breathing. That is the entire range of options available to me.
If you've something to say to me, say it to my face.
I've been saying it to your back for three days. You haven't turned round once.
They're telling it in the villages now. "{deed}"
That's a better story than the one we were in. Leave it be.
{fallen} would have hated this stretch.
{fallen} hated every stretch. That was most of the charm of them.
Set the pace slower. You're favouring that side and you think nobody's watching.
...Slower, then.
You're bleeding.
It isn't mine.
Some of it is.
That went well.
That went quickly. They're not the same thing, and one day the difference is going to matter.
You put yourself between me and the second one.
You'd have done it.
I'd have thought about it first. That's the part I'm turning over.
You broke the line.
I broke the line because the line was about to have you killed in it.
Sit down before you fall down. I'll do the looking about.
I'm fine standing.
You are not, and I'd rather argue with you sitting.
First proper roof in a while.
Don't get used to it. I've got used to things before.
Tell the one about the ferryman again.
You've heard it.
I've heard your version. It gets a boat longer every time and I want to see where it ends.
...It was a barge, by the end. Sit down.
Somebody in the taproom was telling it wrong. "{deed}"
Did you correct them?
No. Their version had us braver in it.
You've taken the good side of the fire again.
I got here first. That's the whole of the system and it has served us well.
There's a place at this fire nobody's sitting in.
I noticed. I've been not-looking at it for an hour.
Say their name, then. {fallen}. It's easier the second time.
{fallen}. ...It isn't, but go on and I'll keep up.
We should say something.
We said it at the time. They heard the version that mattered.
The ground's settled. It looks like it's always been here.
Give it a year and somebody will walk past without slowing down.
Then we'll slow down twice, and it'll come out even.
{fallen} would have hated this. All of us stood about being solemn.
They'd have told us to get on. Loudly, and about four times.
Then let's get on. That's the eulogy they'd have picked.
You've not said a word since we put the stone in.
No.
Right. I'll be over there, then, saying nothing at you.
Do you think they knew? At the end of it.
I think they were busy. I've decided that's a mercy and I'm not revisiting it.
They'd want to hear it. "{deed}"
Say it louder, then. It's a quiet spot and they were never one for quiet.
Somebody's been here. There's cut flowers, and they're not old.
Then they're better at this than we are. Let's not tread on them.
I want mine somewhere with a view.
You'll be dead. The view is wasted.
It's not for me. It's so whoever's digging gets something out of the afternoon.
Sit still. You're pulling it open every time you reach for the pot.
Then pass me the pot.
That is a much better solution than the one I was building up to. Here.
What did you do, before? Actually before.
Nothing that comes up.
It's come up. It's the fire, that's what it's for.
...Fences. I put in fences. And I was good at it, so don't start.
This wood's green. It'll spit all night.
Then we'll be awake all night, and nothing will come at us out of the dark.
That's either very clever or you picked bad wood and won't say.
You've been counting the coin again.
Somebody has to, and it isn't going to be the one who spent it.
If we came into money — real money — what would you do?
Buy a bed. A specific bed. I've thought about this more than is healthy.
Go on then. Describe the bed.
It's a bed. It's indoors. That's the whole of the fantasy and I'm not ashamed.
Word's got ahead of us again. "{deed}"
Is that good?
It's early. Ask me at the next town, when I've seen who crosses the road.
I keep the watch. You slept badly.
I slept fine.
You said a name twice and it wasn't mine. Lie down.
Your turn to cook.
It was my turn last night.
It was, and that's precisely why I'd like you to have another go at it.
That one was avoidable.
So was saying so.
What's the plan, then. Honestly.
Get to {place}. After that I've got nothing and I'd rather not pretend.
Good. I trust that more than a plan.
Give me your boots.
Why.
Because you've been walking wrong for two days and I'd like to know which of us is at fault.
There's a light out east. Been there an hour.
Somebody else's fire.
That's what I thought. Odd, to find that comforting.
I've been keeping a list. Of things I'd tell somebody, if there were somebody.
There's me.
You're on the list. That's the trouble with the list.
You could take the far side of the fire.
I could.
I'm not going to, but I appreciate you laying it out so clearly.
{fallen} used to bank it up like that. Same way, every night.
I know. That's where I learnt it.
How long since we slept somewhere we weren't listening?
I'd have to count, and I'd rather go on not knowing.
Sing something.
No.
Hum it, then. I only want to know if it's the sad one.
...It's the sad one. They're all the sad one.
Show me. Now, not at the fire.
It's shallow.
Everything's shallow until it's a week old and you're grey. Show me.
Anyone counting?
I stopped. It was making me a person I didn't want to be by suppertime.
That was close.
It was not close.
You went down on one knee.
I was checking the ground. Tactically.
You were slow on the left.
And you were nowhere at all, so let's call it even and walk.
One of them was younger than me.
You don't know that.
No. I've decided not to know it. It's working, mostly.
Good throw, that last one.
I was aiming at the other one.
Then it was a superb throw and we'll never speak of it again.
Do we bury them?
We haven't the light, and they had friends who'll come looking.
Then we move. I don't want to be the thing those friends find.
That's twice this week I've pulled you out.
Then stop counting, or start asking for wages.
This'll get told wrong too, you know. Like "{deed}".
Let it. The wrong version's shorter and I've a long way to walk.
You put yourself between me and that.
I was closer.
You were not closer. You moved to be closer.
Then I was closer. Look at the state of my arm and let it go.
Every milestone out here's been chipped off.
Somebody didn't want to be found. Or didn't want us finding them.
Name three things you miss.
Bread. Doors. Being bored.
Bored. That's a good one. I'd forgotten bored was available.
The birds have stopped.
I noticed a while back. I was hoping you hadn't.
This isn't the way.
It's a way.
That is the most expensive sentence you've ever said to me.
Old cart tracks, and they only go one direction.
So whatever left, left loaded, and nothing's come back for the rest of it.
If I go down out here, don't carry me. Just the sword.
I'll carry you and the sword, and complain the whole way, and you'll have to listen.
Slow up. You're favouring it.
We've light left.
We've light left because we're slowing up. That's how the light works.
Someone's been through here inside a day.
Ahead of us or behind us?
I'd like it to be ahead. I'm going to say ahead.
We could have taken the coin and gone home.
Whose home?
That is exactly the answer I didn't want and precisely the one I expected.
{place}, is it? I'd pictured it bigger.
Everything's bigger from a long way off. That's most of why people set out.
You walk on the outside of me. Every road. You think I've not clocked it.
Habit.
It's a good habit. Carry on.
We're four, and we walk like we're five. Still leaving the gap.
{fallen} would've filled it by now with talking. Let it stay empty a bit longer.

reflections.text: You'll have heard by now — {deed}. That was us. I'm still deciding how I feel about it.
People keep telling the story back to us wrong. {deed}, they say, as if it were tidy. It wasn't.
Word runs faster than we walk. {deed}, and here we are, hearing about ourselves in a stranger's mouth.
{fallen} would have had something to say about all this. Probably something unhelpful, and probably right.
We buried {fallen} and kept walking. That's the part nobody puts in the songs — the walking after.
I still count us wrong. Every morning I count one too many, and then I remember {fallen}.
{friend} pulled me out of a fight I had no business being in. I've not found the words for it yet, so I'm using these ones.
Whatever happens here, {friend} and I have come through worse standing closer together.
That's {battles} fields we've walked off, and I remember the ground better than the reasons.
{battles} of them now. I used to be sick after. I'd rather have kept that, if I'm honest.
Somewhere behind us are {battles} fields where somebody's son didn't get up. I'd like this to be worth that.
Every floor of that tower we climb, the air gets older. I don't think it's meant to be breathed by us.
We are {floors} floors up a thing that was built to keep people out. Nobody has said yet what it was keeping in.
I could draw this country from memory now. Every ford, every bad hill. I'd rather have learnt it some other way.
We came in here bleeding and we're standing about making conversation. That's the trade, I suppose.
There are more of us than there were. I keep waiting to be told which one of us is the mistake.
We're carrying enough coin to buy a farm, and not one of us has said the word out loud.
{place}. Another one. They start to run together, and then one of them turns out to matter.
Say what you like about the road — it hasn't finished with us yet, and I've stopped expecting it to.
There's a version of "{deed}" going round where I come off well. I've not corrected anyone, and that's its own small crime.
"{deed}" — that's what they'll put on it. Four words for a whole bad afternoon.
I still set out {fallen}'s bowl. Two weeks now. I've stopped pretending it's absent-mindedness.
The worst of it is how ordinary the morning after was. Same bread. Same weather. {fallen} just wasn't in it.
I've started telling {fallen} things at the end of the day. Out loud, once. I'd rather nobody heard, and I'd rather keep doing it.
{friend} has been wrong about almost everything since we met and right about the only two that counted.
I don't know what {friend} makes of me. I've decided that not asking is a kind of courage.
If it came to it, {friend} would go back for me. I know that the way you know the ground is there.
Two fields, and I can still tell you what the light was doing at both. I'm told that stops.
{battles}. At some point the number stopped meaning fights and started meaning me.
{floors} floors. Whatever's at the top has had a long while to hear us coming.
I've stopped counting down to the top. I count up from the door, so there's always been a door.
A hundred-odd miles of it now, and not one of them felt like progress at the time.
There's country behind us I'll never see again and didn't look at properly the once.
Everyone's carrying something. Nobody's said so. That'll hold until it very suddenly doesn't.
Two of us. That's not a company, that's a habit, and I'd defend it in front of anyone.
Three of us, and we've worked out who talks in the morning and who doesn't. That took longer than the fighting did.
Enough coin to stop for a season. Nobody's suggested it. I'd like to know which of us says it first.
We could buy the inn. Both inns. And we'll spend it on arrows, because that is apparently who we are.
I keep expecting somebody to arrive and tell us we're doing this wrong. Nobody's come. That's worse.
There's a version of me that turned back at the first gate. I think about him. I don't envy him, quite.
Nobody set out to be this. You take one job in {place}, and then the next one is already waiting.
